en: The Banaue Rice Terraces act as giant inclined planes, reducing the effort needed for Ifugao farmers to carry heavy harvests up the mountain.
Rubber tsinelas provide high friction against wet bathroom tiles, preventing slips by increasing the roughness between the foot and the floor.
Gravity pulls ripe Carabao mangoes straight down to the ground when they detach from the branch, regardless of the tree's height.
Filipino fishermen use magnetic compasses on their wooden bangka boats to navigate the open sea when there are no visible landmarks.
The MakBan geothermal power plant in Laguna converts natural underground heat into electrical energy to supply electricity to millions of homes.
Fireflies along the Loboc River in Bohol produce cold light through a chemical reaction in their abdomens to attract mates without generating heat.
Tourists hear a distinct echo when shouting inside the Puerto Princesa Underground River because sound waves bounce off the hard limestone walls.
A traditional clay palayok conducts heat slowly and evenly, making it ideal for simmering Filipino sinigang without burning the bottom.
A coconut hanging high on a palm tree possesses gravitational potential energy that converts to kinetic energy as it falls.
The sharp, V-shaped blade of an itak acts as a wedge to split thick coconut husks into smaller pieces with less force.
Eating a sweet Latundan banana gives a student chemical energy that their muscles convert into kinetic energy while playing patintero.
The wooden kariton uses wheel and axle simple machines to reduce friction, allowing vendors to push heavy loads of street food easily.
